newsitem.title: USA: IMM yen and marks end higher, but off day's peaks.
newsitem.headline: IMM yen and marks end higher, but off day's peaks.

text.p: IMM yen, mark and Swiss franc futures closed sharply higher but off the day's peaks after U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin reiterated that the U.S. favors a strong dollar, traders said.

September marks rallied to $0.5916 around midsession after touching off buy-stop orders near the 50-day moving average of $0.5908. September yen inched above $0.009030, as the dollar continued to sell off from overnight levels.
While yen futures are expected to continue their ascent in the long-term, the rally in marks and Swiss francs were viewed by currency analysts as a short-term phenomena.
"The dollar is really split between the EMU (European monetary union) confusion, and the trade issues with Japan," one currency futures analyst said.
Regarding marks, they said traders and dealers were forced to buy back the currency against the dollar after France decided to review the European Union's budget stability pact.
The decision by the new French government immediately cast fresh doubts on the start of the euro.
"The realization is becoming more and more apparent that there will be a lot of maneuvering to get this thing going," one currency market analyst said.
Some currency market analysts were even more pessimistic on the fate of the EMU, with most expecting that the plans for a single European currency will be eventually scratched.
"It's going to crack," one currency futures trader said.
Many currency analysts said further political wrangling over the EMU will support the dollar against most European currencies in the long run.
The technicals also support this outlook, according to one technical analyst. He said both September marks and Swiss francs remain in a downtrend, despite their strong rallies.

He said September marks would have close above $0.6050, the 2-1/4-month high, to turn their trend higher. September Swiss francs would have to rise and close above the May 20 high of $0.7330 to change their technical outlook.
"The contract had a really bad break," he said, referring to September Swissie's fall to $0.6900, the five-week low, on Friday, from $0.7330 on May 20.
Meanwhile, September yen is poised to move higher, with its next major resistance level at $0.009260, the 6-1/2-month high, he said.

Expectations the interest rate differential between the U.S. and Japan will narrow, coupled with concerns about the U.S.'s trade deficit against Japan are some of the fundamentals supporting yen futures, they said.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was up $0.000122 at $0.008971, marks were up $0.0065 at $0.5898, Swiss francs were $0.0059 higher at $0.7033, sterling was up $0.0034 at $1.6320, Canadian dollars were down $0.0024 at $0.7255, Australian dollars were $0.0008 lower at $0.7625 and Mexican pesos were $0.000300 higher at $0.119850.
